instruction:
# ERP — HRM & Time Tracking Platform

## Organization (Multi-Tenancy)

- The platform supports multiple organizations (multi-tenancy)
- Each organization operates independently with its own employees, projects, and data
- Users create an organization during initial sign-up
- Each organization has: name, description, logo image, currency (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW), timezone, and fiscal start month
- Organization owners can edit organization settings
- Organization owners can delete their organization only if:
  - All pending timesheets are resolved (approved or rejected)
  - There are no active employee contracts
- When an organization is deleted:
  - All employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets are permanently deleted
  - The owner's account remains but is no longer associated with any organization

## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- A user can belong to multiple organizations
- When logging in, users select which organization to work in (organization context)
- All subsequent actions are scoped to the selected organization
- Users can switch organizations without logging out
- Users can delete their account:
  - If they are the sole owner of an organization, they must transfer ownership or delete the organization first
  - Their employee records in other organizations are marked as "deactivated"

## User Profile

- Each user has a global profile with: display name, avatar image, phone number
- Users can edit their profile
- Profile is shared across all organizations the user belongs to

## Roles and Permissions

- Each organization has its own set of roles
- Three built-in roles (cannot be deleted):
  - **Owner**: full access to all features, can manage roles and members
  - **Manager**: can manage employees, projects, approve timesheets, view reports
  - **Employee**: can track time, submit timesheets, view own data
- Organization owners can create custom roles
- Each custom role has: name and a set of permissions
- Available permissions:
  - `org:manage` — edit organization settings
  - `employee:manage` — add, edit, deactivate employees
  - `employee:view` — view employee list and details
  - `project:manage` — create, edit, delete projects and tasks
  - `project:view` — view projects and tasks
  - `time:manage` — edit or delete any employee's timelogs
  - `time:approve` — approve or reject timesheets
  - `time:view_all` — view all employees' timelogs and timesheets
  - `report:view` — view organization reports
- Organization owners can edit custom roles
- Organization owners can delete custom roles only if no employees are assigned to them
- Each employee in an organization is assigned exactly one role
- Role assignment can be changed by users with `employee:manage` permission

## Employee Management

- Users with `employee:manage` permission can invite new employees to the organization
- Invitation is done by email
- If the invited email already has an account, the user is added to the organization
- If the invited email has no account, a pending invitation is created
  - When the user signs up with that email, they are automatically added to the pending organizations
- Each employee record has:
  - Reference to the user account
  - Role in this organization
  - Department (optional)
  - Position/title (optional)
  - Employment type: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern
  - Status: active, deactivated
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit employee records (department, position, employment type)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can deactivate employees
  - Deactivated employees cannot log time or submit timesheets
  - Deactivated employees' historical data (timelogs, timesheets) is preserved
  - Deactivated employees can be reactivated
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view the employee list
- The employee list is paginated
- Employees can filter the list by: department, employment type, status
- Employees can search by name

## Employee Contracts

- Each employee can have multiple contracts (historical record)
- Only one contract can be active at a time
- Each contract has:
  - Start date (required)
  - End date (optional, null means ongoing)
  - Pay rate (required, numeric value)
  - Pay period: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly
  - Working hours per week (required, e.g., 40)
  - Notes (optional)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can create contracts for employees
- Creating a new contract automatically ends the previous active contract (sets end date to the day before the new contract starts)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit the current active contract
- Past contracts cannot be edited (immutable historical record)
- Employees can view their own contracts
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view any employee's contracts

## Departments

- Each organization can have departments
- Each department has: name, description, and optional parent department (one level of nesting)
- Users with `org:manage` permission can create, edit, and delete departments
- Deleting a department sets employees' department to null (does not delete employees)
- Employees can view the list of departments

## Projects

- Users with `project:manage` permission can create projects
- Each project has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Color code (for UI display, required)
  - Status: active, archived, completed
  - Budget hours (optional, total estimated hours)
  - Start date (optional)
  - End date (optional)
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit projects
- Users with `project:manage` permission can archive or complete projects
  - Archived/completed projects cannot receive new timelogs
  - Existing timelogs on archived/completed projects are preserved
- Users with `project:manage` permission can delete projects only if:
  - The project has no timelogs associated with it
- Users with `project:view` permission can view all projects
- The project list is paginated
- Projects can be filtered by status

## Project Members

- Users with `project:manage` permission can assign employees to projects
- An employee can be assigned to multiple projects
- Each project membership has: employee, project, and assigned role (member or project-lead)
- Project leads can manage tasks within their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can remove employees from projects
- Employees can view which projects they are assigned to

## Tasks

- Project leads or users with `project:manage` permission can create tasks within a project
- Each task has:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Status: open, in-progress, completed, closed
  - Priority: low, medium, high, urgent
  - Estimated hours (optional)
  - Due date (optional)
  - Assigned employee (optional, must be a project member)
  - Parent task (optional, for subtasks — one level of nesting only)
- Project leads can edit tasks in their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit any task
- Task status changes are recorded in task history
- Each task history entry records: timestamp, old status, new status, who made the change
- Employees can view tasks in projects they are assigned to
- Tasks can be filtered by: status, priority, assigned employee
- Tasks can be sorted by: due date, priority, creation date

## Time Tracking — Timelogs

- Employees can log time entries (timelogs)
- Each timelog has:
  - Date (required)
  - Duration in minutes (required)
  - Project (required, must be a project the employee is assigned to)
  - Task (optional, must belong to the selected project)
  - Description (optional, what was done)
  - Billable flag (boolean, default true)
- Employees can only create timelogs for themselves
- Employees can edit their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of an approved timesheet
- Employees can delete their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of any submitted or approved timesheet
- Users with `time:manage` permission can edit or delete any employee's timelogs
- Users with `time:view_all` permission can view all employees' timelogs
- Employees can view their own timelogs
- Timelogs are paginated
- Timelogs can be filtered by: date range, project, task, billable status

## Time Tracking — Timesheets

- A timesheet is a collection of timelogs for a specific week (Monday to Sunday)
- Employees submit timesheets for approval
- Each timesheet has:
  - Employee (owner)
  - Week start date (Monday)
  - Week end date (Sunday)
  - Status: draft, submitted, approved, rejected
  - Total hours (calculated from included timelogs)
  - Submitted at (timestamp)
  - Reviewed at (timestamp, when approved/rejected)
  - Reviewed by (the user who approved/rejected)
  - Rejection reason (text, required when rejecting)
- Employees can create a draft timesheet for a specific week
- Creating a draft automatically includes all timelogs for that employee in that week
- Employees can add or remove timelogs from a draft timesheet
- Employees can submit a draft timesheet for approval
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if it has no timelogs
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if another timesheet for the same week is already submitted or approved
- Users with `time:approve` permission can view all submitted timesheets
- Users with `time:approve` permission can approve submitted timesheets
  - Approved timesheets lock all included timelogs (cannot be edited or deleted)
- Users with `time:approve` permission can reject submitted timesheets with a reason
  - Rejected timesheets return to draft status
  - The employee can modify and resubmit the rejected timesheet
- Employees can view their own timesheets
- Timesheets are paginated
- Timesheets can be filtered by: status, date range

## Timer (Live Time Tracking)

- Employees can start a timer to track time in real-time
- Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time
- Starting a timer requires selecting a project (task is optional)
- The timer records: start timestamp, project, task, description
- Employees can stop their timer
  - Stopping the timer creates a timelog with the calculated duration
  - Duration is rounded to the nearest minute
- Employees can discard their timer (no timelog is created)
- Employees can view their currently running timer
- If an employee forgets to stop their timer, it continues running indefinitely (no automatic stop)
- Employees can edit the description and project/task of a running timer

## Reports

- Users with `report:view` permission can access organization reports
- Available reports:

**Time Report**
- Shows total hours logged per employee for a given date range
- Can be grouped by: employee, project, task
- Can be filtered by: date range, employee, project, billable status
- Shows breakdown: total hours, billable hours, non-billable hours

**Project Budget Report**
- Shows each project's budget hours vs. actual hours logged
- Shows percentage of budget consumed
- Projects without budget hours are excluded

**Weekly Summary Report**
- Shows a week-by-week summary for a given date range
- Each week shows: total hours, number of timelogs, number of employees who logged time
- Can be filtered by project

## Activity Log

- The system records significant actions as activity log entries
- Each activity log entry has: timestamp, user who performed the action, action type, target entity, and details
- Logged actions include:
  - Employee invited, deactivated, reactivated
  - Contract created or edited
  - Project created, archived, completed, deleted
  - Task status changed
  - Timesheet submitted, approved, rejected
  - Role assigned or changed
- Users with `org:manage` permission can view the full activity log
- The activity log is paginated
- The activity log can be filtered by: action type, user, date range

## Dashboard

- Each employee has a personal dashboard showing:
  - Hours logged today
  - Hours logged this week
  - Active timer status (if running)
  - Recent timelogs (last 5)
  - Pending timesheet status for current week
  - Tasks assigned to them with status "in-progress" or "open"

- Users with `report:view` permission see an organization dashboard showing:
  - Total employees (active)
  - Total hours logged this week (all employees)
  - Number of pending timesheets awaiting approval
  - Projects with budget utilization over 80%
  - Top 5 employees by hours logged this week

## Data Isolation

- All data is strictly isolated per organization
- Employees in one organization cannot see data from another organization
- Users who belong to multiple organizations only see data for their currently selected organization
- API endpoints enforce organization context on every request

scenario.draft:
Test that an employee with an existing active timer receives 409 Conflict when attempting to start another timer.

**Setup sequence:**
1. Register a new member via `/erpHrm/auth/member/join`

2. Call POST `/erpHrm/member/timers` with second project's ID - expect 409 Conflict

**Validation points:**
- First timer creation returns 201 Created
- Second timer creation returns 409 Conflict status (not 400 or 500)
- Error message indicates 'An active timer already exists'
- Verify first timer is still active via GET `/erpHrm/member/timers`
- Employee cannot start new timer until existing one is stopped or discarded

scenario.draft:
Test retrieving the currently running timer for an authenticated employee who has an active timer.

Prerequisites: Create a member account via /auth/member/join. The authenticated member must have an active employee record in the organization. Start a timer by calling POST /erpHrm/member/timers with a valid project ID and optional task.

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as the member via /auth/member/join
2. Start a timer by calling POST /erpHrm/member/timers with erpHrmProjectId set to a project the employee is assigned to
3. Wait a few seconds to allow elapsed time to accumulate
4. Call GET /erpHrm/member/timers to retrieve the active timer

Validation Points:
- Response status code should be 200
- Response body should contain timer details matching the created timer
- Response should include: id (UUID), startedAt (ISO timestamp), description (nullable), elapsed (calculated seconds since start), project (with id, name, color), task (nullable, with id and title if set)
- Elapsed time should be greater than 0 and increasing over time
- The project object should contain the project that was selected when starting the timer
- If a task was selected when starting the timer, the task object should be present with task details

scenario.draft:
Test scenario for successfully switching organization context between two organizations.

**Setup**:
1. Authenticate as admin to create the organizational structure
2. Create two organizations (Org A and Org B)
3. Register a member and authenticate as member
4. Create employee records for the member in both organizations via admin

**Test Steps**:
1. Call POST /erpHrm/member/organization-context with Org A's organizationId
2. Verify response returns 200 OK with IErpHrmOrganizationContext containing Org A details
3. Verify employee record shows member's role and permissions in Org A
4. Switch to Org B by calling the same endpoint with Org B's organizationId
5. Verify response returns 200 OK with Org B details and Org B permissions
6. Confirm subsequent API calls are scoped to the selected organization

**Expected Results**:
- 200 OK with complete organization context including nested organization, employee, and permissions objects
- Each organization switch returns the correct role-specific permissions for that organization

scenario.draft:
Test that an authenticated admin can successfully retrieve the complete list of available permissions in the system.

Steps:
1. Register a new admin account via POST /erpHrm/auth/admin/join with email, password, and displayName
2. Extract the JWT access token from the response
3. Send GET request to /erpHrm/admin/permissions with Bearer token authorization
4. Validate HTTP 200 response status
5. Verify response body contains items array with IErpHrmRolePermission objects
6. Validate each item has required fields: id (UUID), permission (string), role (object with id, name, isBuiltin), createdAt, updatedAt
7. Verify that permission codes follow the pattern 'resource:action' (e.g., 'org:manage', 'employee:manage')

This is the primary success path for permission list retrieval.

Test retrieving project member analytics when the project has members assigned.

Steps:
1. Register a member account using POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join

- Each member in the array should have assigned_role, created_at, and employee information

scenario.draft: Test retrieving task analytics for a project where the authenticated member has been assigned as a project member. First authenticate as a member, then create a project, and assign the member to that project. After setup, call the analytics endpoint with the project ID. Verify the response contains: totalTasks (0 initially), statusBreakdown with all four statuses (open, in-progress, completed, closed) set to 0, priorityBreakdown with all four levels (low, medium, high, urgent) set to 0, completionRate of 0 (since no tasks exist), averageEstimatedHours as null (no tasks with estimates), overdueTasks as 0, and temporalTrend as an empty array. This validates the endpoint works correctly for a project with no tasks. The project membership assignment is critical because the endpoint requires project:view or project:manage permission which is granted through project membership.

scenario.draft: Test that a member who is not assigned to a project cannot access its task analytics. Authenticate as first member, create a project, and assign only the first member to it. Then authenticate as a second member who is not assigned to this project. Attempt to call the analytics endpoint with the project ID as the second member. The system should reject this request with a 403 Forbidden error, as the second member has no project membership or project:view/project:manage permission for this project. This validates the data isolation principle where employees can only view analytics for projects they are assigned to. The second member should receive an error response indicating insufficient permissions to access the project analytics.

Test scenario for generating a weekly summary report across multiple weeks with timelog data.

**Setup**: Admin authenticates, then creates an organization with employees and projects. Create timelogs spanning multiple complete weeks (Monday-Sunday) with varying hours and employee distributions.

**Test execution**:
1. Authenticate as admin using /auth/admin/join
2. Create organization context using /admin/organizations

**Validation points**:

- Week 2 shows correct aggregation: totalHours=20, timelogsCount=2, employeesCount=1
- Results are ordered by weekStartDate ascending
- Pagination metadata is present with correct records count (2)
- Partial weeks at boundaries are NOT included

Test accepting a valid pending organization invitation as an authenticated member. This validates the primary success path for invitation acceptance workflow.

- Invitation status transitions from 'pending' to 'accepted'
- Verify the returned invitation contains correct email, organization, and status

instruction:
# ERP — HRM & Time Tracking Platform

## Organization (Multi-Tenancy)

- The platform supports multiple organizations (multi-tenancy)
- Each organization operates independently with its own employees, projects, and data
- Users create an organization during initial sign-up
- Each organization has: name, description, logo image, currency (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW), timezone, and fiscal start month
- Organization owners can edit organization settings
- Organization owners can delete their organization only if:
  - All pending timesheets are resolved (approved or rejected)
  - There are no active employee contracts
- When an organization is deleted:
  - All employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets are permanently deleted
  - The owner's account remains but is no longer associated with any organization

## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- A user can belong to multiple organizations
- When logging in, users select which organization to work in (organization context)
- All subsequent actions are scoped to the selected organization
- Users can switch organizations without logging out
- Users can delete their account:
  - If they are the sole owner of an organization, they must transfer ownership or delete the organization first
  - Their employee records in other organizations are marked as "deactivated"

## User Profile

- Each user has a global profile with: display name, avatar image, phone number
- Users can edit their profile
- Profile is shared across all organizations the user belongs to

## Roles and Permissions

- Each organization has its own set of roles
- Three built-in roles (cannot be deleted):
  - **Owner**: full access to all features, can manage roles and members
  - **Manager**: can manage employees, projects, approve timesheets, view reports
  - **Employee**: can track time, submit timesheets, view own data
- Organization owners can create custom roles
- Each custom role has: name and a set of permissions
- Available permissions:
  - `org:manage` — edit organization settings
  - `employee:manage` — add, edit, deactivate employees
  - `employee:view` — view employee list and details
  - `project:manage` — create, edit, delete projects and tasks
  - `project:view` — view projects and tasks
  - `time:manage` — edit or delete any employee's timelogs
  - `time:approve` — approve or reject timesheets
  - `time:view_all` — view all employees' timelogs and timesheets
  - `report:view` — view organization reports
- Organization owners can edit custom roles
- Organization owners can delete custom roles only if no employees are assigned to them
- Each employee in an organization is assigned exactly one role
- Role assignment can be changed by users with `employee:manage` permission

## Employee Management

- Users with `employee:manage` permission can invite new employees to the organization
- Invitation is done by email
- If the invited email already has an account, the user is added to the organization
- If the invited email has no account, a pending invitation is created
  - When the user signs up with that email, they are automatically added to the pending organizations
- Each employee record has:
  - Reference to the user account
  - Role in this organization
  - Department (optional)
  - Position/title (optional)
  - Employment type: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern
  - Status: active, deactivated
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit employee records (department, position, employment type)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can deactivate employees
  - Deactivated employees cannot log time or submit timesheets
  - Deactivated employees' historical data (timelogs, timesheets) is preserved
  - Deactivated employees can be reactivated
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view the employee list
- The employee list is paginated
- Employees can filter the list by: department, employment type, status
- Employees can search by name

## Employee Contracts

- Each employee can have multiple contracts (historical record)
- Only one contract can be active at a time
- Each contract has:
  - Start date (required)
  - End date (optional, null means ongoing)
  - Pay rate (required, numeric value)
  - Pay period: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly
  - Working hours per week (required, e.g., 40)
  - Notes (optional)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can create contracts for employees
- Creating a new contract automatically ends the previous active contract (sets end date to the day before the new contract starts)
- Users with `employee:manage` permission can edit the current active contract
- Past contracts cannot be edited (immutable historical record)
- Employees can view their own contracts
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view any employee's contracts

## Departments

- Each organization can have departments
- Each department has: name, description, and optional parent department (one level of nesting)
- Users with `org:manage` permission can create, edit, and delete departments
- Deleting a department sets employees' department to null (does not delete employees)
- Employees can view the list of departments

## Projects

- Users with `project:manage` permission can create projects
- Each project has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Color code (for UI display, required)
  - Status: active, archived, completed
  - Budget hours (optional, total estimated hours)
  - Start date (optional)
  - End date (optional)
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit projects
- Users with `project:manage` permission can archive or complete projects
  - Archived/completed projects cannot receive new timelogs
  - Existing timelogs on archived/completed projects are preserved
- Users with `project:manage` permission can delete projects only if:
  - The project has no timelogs associated with it
- Users with `project:view` permission can view all projects
- The project list is paginated
- Projects can be filtered by status

## Project Members

- Users with `project:manage` permission can assign employees to projects
- An employee can be assigned to multiple projects
- Each project membership has: employee, project, and assigned role (member or project-lead)
- Project leads can manage tasks within their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can remove employees from projects
- Employees can view which projects they are assigned to

## Tasks

- Project leads or users with `project:manage` permission can create tasks within a project
- Each task has:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Status: open, in-progress, completed, closed
  - Priority: low, medium, high, urgent
  - Estimated hours (optional)
  - Due date (optional)
  - Assigned employee (optional, must be a project member)
  - Parent task (optional, for subtasks — one level of nesting only)
- Project leads can edit tasks in their project
- Users with `project:manage` permission can edit any task
- Task status changes are recorded in task history
- Each task history entry records: timestamp, old status, new status, who made the change
- Employees can view tasks in projects they are assigned to
- Tasks can be filtered by: status, priority, assigned employee
- Tasks can be sorted by: due date, priority, creation date

## Time Tracking — Timelogs

- Employees can log time entries (timelogs)
- Each timelog has:
  - Date (required)
  - Duration in minutes (required)
  - Project (required, must be a project the employee is assigned to)
  - Task (optional, must belong to the selected project)
  - Description (optional, what was done)
  - Billable flag (boolean, default true)
- Employees can only create timelogs for themselves
- Employees can edit their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of an approved timesheet
- Employees can delete their own timelogs only if:
  - The timelog is not part of any submitted or approved timesheet
- Users with `time:manage` permission can edit or delete any employee's timelogs
- Users with `time:view_all` permission can view all employees' timelogs
- Employees can view their own timelogs
- Timelogs are paginated
- Timelogs can be filtered by: date range, project, task, billable status

## Time Tracking — Timesheets

- A timesheet is a collection of timelogs for a specific week (Monday to Sunday)
- Employees submit timesheets for approval
- Each timesheet has:
  - Employee (owner)
  - Week start date (Monday)
  - Week end date (Sunday)
  - Status: draft, submitted, approved, rejected
  - Total hours (calculated from included timelogs)
  - Submitted at (timestamp)
  - Reviewed at (timestamp, when approved/rejected)
  - Reviewed by (the user who approved/rejected)
  - Rejection reason (text, required when rejecting)
- Employees can create a draft timesheet for a specific week
- Creating a draft automatically includes all timelogs for that employee in that week
- Employees can add or remove timelogs from a draft timesheet
- Employees can submit a draft timesheet for approval
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if it has no timelogs
  - A timesheet cannot be submitted if another timesheet for the same week is already submitted or approved
- Users with `time:approve` permission can view all submitted timesheets
- Users with `time:approve` permission can approve submitted timesheets
  - Approved timesheets lock all included timelogs (cannot be edited or deleted)
- Users with `time:approve` permission can reject submitted timesheets with a reason
  - Rejected timesheets return to draft status
  - The employee can modify and resubmit the rejected timesheet
- Employees can view their own timesheets
- Timesheets are paginated
- Timesheets can be filtered by: status, date range

## Timer (Live Time Tracking)

- Employees can start a timer to track time in real-time
- Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time
- Starting a timer requires selecting a project (task is optional)
- The timer records: start timestamp, project, task, description
- Employees can stop their timer
  - Stopping the timer creates a timelog with the calculated duration
  - Duration is rounded to the nearest minute
- Employees can discard their timer (no timelog is created)
- Employees can view their currently running timer
- If an employee forgets to stop their timer, it continues running indefinitely (no automatic stop)
- Employees can edit the description and project/task of a running timer

## Reports

- Users with `report:view` permission can access organization reports
- Available reports:

**Time Report**
- Shows total hours logged per employee for a given date range
- Can be grouped by: employee, project, task
- Can be filtered by: date range, employee, project, billable status
- Shows breakdown: total hours, billable hours, non-billable hours

**Project Budget Report**
- Shows each project's budget hours vs. actual hours logged
- Shows percentage of budget consumed
- Projects without budget hours are excluded

**Weekly Summary Report**
- Shows a week-by-week summary for a given date range
- Each week shows: total hours, number of timelogs, number of employees who logged time
- Can be filtered by project

## Activity Log

- The system records significant actions as activity log entries
- Each activity log entry has: timestamp, user who performed the action, action type, target entity, and details
- Logged actions include:
  - Employee invited, deactivated, reactivated
  - Contract created or edited
  - Project created, archived, completed, deleted
  - Task status changed
  - Timesheet submitted, approved, rejected
  - Role assigned or changed
- Users with `org:manage` permission can view the full activity log
- The activity log is paginated
- The activity log can be filtered by: action type, user, date range

## Dashboard

- Each employee has a personal dashboard showing:
  - Hours logged today
  - Hours logged this week
  - Active timer status (if running)
  - Recent timelogs (last 5)
  - Pending timesheet status for current week
  - Tasks assigned to them with status "in-progress" or "open"

- Users with `report:view` permission see an organization dashboard showing:
  - Total employees (active)
  - Total hours logged this week (all employees)
  - Number of pending timesheets awaiting approval
  - Projects with budget utilization over 80%
  - Top 5 employees by hours logged this week

## Data Isolation

- All data is strictly isolated per organization
- Employees in one organization cannot see data from another organization
- Users who belong to multiple organizations only see data for their currently selected organization
- API endpoints enforce organization context on every request

plan.thinking: IErpHrmOrganization.ICreate is a Create DTO for organization creation. Maps directly to erp_hrm_organizations table based on x-autobe-database-schema annotation. The owner_id field is not in the Create DTO body but comes from the authenticated admin actor via JWT session.

IErpHrmDepartment.ICreate is a Create DTO type that maps to erp_hrm_departments table. Collectable. The organization ID comes from the authorized session context (JWT), not from the request body, making it an external reference. The parentId is included in the DTO body so no external reference needed for parent department.

IErpHrmRole.ICreate is a Create DTO for custom organization roles. Maps to erp_hrm_roles table with permissions stored in erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table. Organization context extracted from authenticated admin session. Collectable.

IErpHrmEmployee.ICreate is a Create DTO for POST /erpHrm/admin/employees endpoint. Maps to erp_hrm_employees table with x-autobe-database-schema annotation. All FK references (roleId, departmentId) are included in the DTO body. Organization context comes from the authorized admin's session. Collectable: Yes.
IErpHrmRolePermission.ICreate is a Create DTO used for assigning permissions to roles. Maps directly to erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table. The roleId path parameter references erp_hrm_roles.

IErpHrmReport.ICreate is a Create DTO (.ICreate suffix) for POST /erpHrm/admin/reports endpoint. Maps to erp_hrm_reports table with nested erp_hrm_report_parameters. Organization_id and member_id references come from the authorized admin session context.

IErpHrmReportParameter.ICreate is a Create DTO that maps to erp_hrm_report_parameters table. It creates filter parameters for a report with a 1:1 relationship to erp_hrm_reports. The erp_hrm_report_id foreign key is provided via path parameter {reportId} in the endpoint /erpHrm/admin/reports/{reportId}/parameters. Collectable with reference to parent report from path parameter.

IErpHrmContract.ICreate is a Create DTO for contracts that maps to erp_hrm_contracts table. The employee_id is sourced from path parameter employeeId, making erp_hrm_employees an external reference. This is a collectable DTO.

IErpHrmProjectMember.ICreate is a Create DTO for assigning employees to projects. Maps to erp_hrm_project_members table with employeeId and assignedRole fields. The projectId FK comes from the path parameter, making erp_hrm_projects an external reference. Collectable.

IErpHrmProject.ICreate is a Create DTO used for POST /erpHrm/admin/projects. The interface schema explicitly maps to erp_hrm_projects table via x-autobe-database-schema. Organization context extracted from admin session - needs erp_hrm_organizations reference.

IErpHrmTask.ICreate is a Create DTO for task creation via POST /erpHrm/admin/projects/{projectId}/tasks. Maps to erp_hrm_tasks table via x-autobe-database-schema. The projectId path parameter provides erp_hrm_project_id FK. Collectable.

IErpHrmTimelog.ICreate is a Create DTO that maps to erp_hrm_timelogs table. The DTO contains projectId, taskId (optional), date, durationMinutes, description, and billable fields. The employee ID is not in the DTO body - it comes from the authenticated session via JWT. References needed: erp_hrm_employees (from authorized actor via session) and erp_hrm_member_sessions (from authorized session).

IErpHrmTimer.ICreate is a Create DTO for starting a timer session. Maps to erp_hrm_timers database table. The DTO contains erpHrmProjectId (required) and erpHrmTaskId (optional) in the body. The erp_hrm_employee_id is derived from the authenticated session context, not from the request body. Collectable.

IErpHrmTimesheet.ICreate is a Create DTO used in POST /erpHrm/member/timesheets to create draft timesheets. Maps directly to erp_hrm_timesheets table with x-autobe-database-schema. The employee and organization context come from authorized session (JWT).

IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate is a Create DTO for creating invitation records. Maps to erp_hrm_invitations table. The organizationId comes from path parameter requiring erp_hrm_organizations reference. Role and department are optional FKs included in DTO body. Collectable.

IErpHrmEmployee is a full employee entity DTO with x-autobe-database-schema: erp_hrm_employees. It maps directly to the employees table and is used for API responses. Contains nested member, organization, role, department relations and HAS-MANY compositions for contracts, projectMemberships, assignedTasks, timelogs, timesheets, timers. Transformable with JOINs.

IErpHrmRolePermission is a role permission assignment DTO. Based on the loaded interface schema, it maps directly to erp_hrm_role_permissions table with columns: id, permission, created_at, updated_at. It also has a BELONGS-TO relation to IErpHrmRole.ISummary. This is a Read DTO used for API responses that maps directly to one database table, making it transformable.

IErpHrmDepartment.IHierarchy is a department hierarchy node for tree structure rendering. Maps directly to erp_hrm_departments table with parent-child recursive relationships. The x-autobe-database-schema property confirms it maps to erp_hrm_departments. Transformable.

IErpHrmRole.ISummary is a summary DTO for role list responses. It maps directly to erp_hrm_roles table with JOIN to erp_hrm_organizations for organization context. This is a Read DTO that is DB-backed with direct mapping to the primary table erp_hrm_roles. Transformable.

IErpHrmRolePermission.IUpdateResult is a read response DTO that aggregates permissions from erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table with role JOIN. The schema explicitly defines x-autobe-database-schema: erp_hrm_role_permissions. This DTO is used for API responses and backed by database queries, meeting the transformable criteria (Read DTO + DB-backed + Direct mapping to junction table).

IErpHrmTimelog.IInvert is a read DTO with x-autobe-database-schema: erp_hrm_timelogs. It maps directly to the erp_hrm_timelogs table with nested employee, project, task, and timesheet relations. This is a DB-backed entity DTO used for API responses. Transformable.

IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary is a read DTO (ISummary variant) for listing employees. The interface schema shows x-autobe-database-schema: erp_hrm_employees. It maps directly to erp_hrm_employees table with JOINs to member, role, and department relations. This is a DB-backed read DTO with direct mapping to one primary table. Transformable.

IErpHrmInvitation.IResendResponse is a read DTO returned after resending an invitation. Maps directly to erp_hrm_invitations table with all properties as direct column mappings. Has BELONGS-TO relations to organization, role, and department. Transformable.

IErpHrmInvitation.ISummary is a read DTO (ISummary variant) that maps directly to erp_hrm_invitations table. It contains direct fields (id, email, status, position, note, accepted_at, expires_at, created_at) and two JOIN relations (role, department). The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms erp_hrm_invitations as the mapped table. Transformable.

IErpHrmInvitation.IVerifyResponse is a read DTO for invitation token verification. Maps to erp_hrm_invitations table with JOINs to organization, role, and department for contextual display. x-autobe-database-schema confirms erp_hrm_invitations as the primary table.

IErpHrmInvitation is a complete invitation entity DTO for API responses. Maps directly to erp_hrm_invitations table with all columns and BELONGS-TO relations to organization, role, and department. Transformable.

IErpHrmRolePermission.IList is a LIST operation that maps to erp_hrm_role_permissions table with JOIN to erp_hrm_roles. The schema has x-autobe-database-schema set to erp_hrm_role_permissions. Data comes directly from database queries with SELECT permission code, role_id, role_name, created_at, updated_at via JOIN. Transformable.

IErpHrmReport.ISummary is a read DTO with x-autobe-database-schema annotation pointing to erp_hrm_reports. It contains id, reportType, name, createdAt fields mapped directly to database columns, plus BELONGS-TO relations to organization and member. This is a transformable DTO.

IErpHrmReport is transformable. It's a read DTO with x-autobe-database-schema: erp_hrm_reports. Maps directly to erp_hrm_reports table with id, report_type, name, created_at, updated_at fields. Contains BELONGS-TO relations (organization, generatedByMember) and HAS-ONE composition (parameter).

IErpHrmAdmin.ISummary is a Read DTO that maps directly to erp_hrm_admins table with properties id, email, displayName, avatarUri, phone, createdAt. All fields map directly to database columns. Transformable.

IErpHrmAdminAuditLog.ISummary is a database-backed read DTO for administrative audit log entries. Maps directly to erp_hrm_admin_audit_logs table with BELONGS-TO relation to erp_hrm_admins returning IErpHrmAdmin.ISummary. Transformable.

IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary is a read DTO for list views and selection interfaces. It has x-autobe-database-schema: erp_hrm_organizations, maps directly to erp_hrm_organizations table with owner JOIN to erp_hrm_members. Transformable.

IErpHrmActivityLog is a complete activity log entry DTO that maps directly to erp_hrm_activity_logs database table. The schema has x-autobe-database-schema: "erp_hrm_activity_logs" with direct field mappings (id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, details, created_at) and JOINs to erp_hrm_members and erp_hrm_organizations. This is a read DTO for API responses that is database-backed with a direct one-to-one mapping to the primary table. Transformable.

IErpHrmMember is a complete member account entity representing a registered user. All properties map directly to erp_hrm_members table columns: id, email, display_name, avatar_uri, phone, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. This is a Read DTO for API responses, database-backed with direct 1:1 mapping. Transformable.

IErpHrmAdminAuditLog is a Read DTO for administrative audit log entries. All its fields map directly to erp_hrm_admin_audit_logs table columns (id, action_type, target_entity, target_id, metadata, ip_address, created_at). The admin field is a BELONGS-TO relation to erp_hrm_admins. This meets all transformable criteria: Read DTO, DB-backed, direct mapping to one primary table.

IErpHrmMember.ISummary is a lightweight member summary for list display. Maps directly to erp_hrm_members table with direct fields: id, email, display_name, avatar_uri, phone, created_at, deleted_at. No JOINs required. Transformable.

IErpHrmMemberSession is a Read DTO representing authenticated member session data. Maps directly to erp_hrm_member_sessions table with direct column mappings (id, ip, href, referrer, tokenExpiredAt, createdAt, expiredAt) and a join to erp_hrm_members for the embedded member summary. Transformable.

IErpHrmAdmin is a Read DTO for administrator accounts. Schema contains x-autobe-database-schema: erp_hrm_admins with direct column mapping for all fields (id, email, display_name, avatar_uri, phone, created_at, updated_at). Excludes password_hash for security. This is a direct database-backed entity with one-to-one table mapping.

IErpHrmOrganization is a complete organization entity DTO used for API responses. This is a read DTO that is DB-backed with direct table mapping. Transformable.

IErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary is a read DTO for activity log entries. Includes a BELONGS-TO join for member returning IErpHrmMember.ISummary. Organization context is filtered via API. This is a database-backed entity with direct table mapping.
